title: I visit one of the most haunted pub's in Norwich to put its reputation to the test
excerpt: Near Norwich Cathedral lies the city's oldest pub - but is it the most haunted? Landlady Rita McCluskey reveals the site's ghostly secrets.
content:
It claims to be Norwich's oldest pub, but could it also be its most haunted? I visited the Adam and Eve to find out.

The Bishopgate site dates to 1249 and has built a reputation not just for its food and drink, but for the ghostly tales that have attracted curious visitors from around the world.

I visited one of the most haunted pubs in Norwich (Image: Submitted)

The pub dates back to 1249 (Image: Submitted)

Armed with my boyfriend Dale, we visited the haunted site on October 24 to uncover the secrets behind the pub.

I was greeted by the landlady of 25 years, Rita McCluskey, who showed us to our table opposite the site's large bar area.

Rita McCluskey (Image: Submitted)

She shared tales of the spirits said to haunt the centuries-old pub and explained why it has been a popular starting point for Norwich Ghost Walks for nearly 30 years.

The spirits said to haunt the site include ghost of Lord Sheffield, a Tudor nobleman who was hacked to death during Kett's Rebellion in 1549.

Ms McCluskey claims customers have reported mysterious taps on the shoulder from unseen hands and keys have vanished without explanation only to reappear later.

The bar area (Image: Submitted)

To my surprise, the pub had a very homely feel, with walls lined with photographs of Ms McCluskey and visitors from years gone by.

The menu features light lunches and hot meals, including pies, sandwiches, and soups and is served from 12-2.30pm every day.

Our food (Image: Submitted)

Roast dinners are served on Sundays (Image: Submitted)

Dale and I enjoyed Ms McCluskey's delicious homemade apple and rhubarb crumble, made with apples grown on site and rhubarb from her garden in Costessey.

Ms McCluskey said she scaled back the menu after Covid as people’s habits had changed.

The site serves roast dinners on Sunday with lashes of gravy and all the trimmings.
